To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of Semantic Web technologies for producing Linked Data for smart cities is a promising approach, but the process of transforming heterogeneous sources is not straightforward.

1) it is possible to integrate heterogeneous data sources in a comprehensive model for smart cities; 2) the use of semantic web technologies and Linked Data can be a viable approach to achieve interoperability in smart cities; 3) domain practitioners and members of the public are willing to contribute and play with the prototype and provide valuable feedbacks.

(1) the use of Linked Data for smart cities can be successfully achieved by means of a comprehensive data model that is able to integrate different sources, and (2) the use of ontology design patterns is a good approach for modeling public transportation and urban fault reporting, but not road maintenance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of Linked Data for Smart City applications.
the design of data models and the implementation of a prototype that can be used as reference practices for the development of smart cities.
the development of a smart city data model and the production of a prototype of a smart city platform based on open data and semantic web technologies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed approach is feasible and scalable, and it is a valuable starting point for the development of a city-wide data model and a prototype for smart city applications, as it is able to address the requirements of both domain experts and general users.
the proposed approach has been successful in terms of data integration and semantic interoperability.
our prototype and data model are a valuable contribution for the community of smart cities, and that they can be easily reused in similar cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed prototype can be a reference for future similar initiatives.
we have shown that it is possible to produce a large-scale Linked Dataset for a city, and that this can be achieved with a limited amount of resources and in a reasonable amount of time.
we have produced Linked Data for smart cities, and that we have done it in a way that is reusable and scalable.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the adoption of Semantic Web technologies can help in achieving the vision of smart cities by providing an interoperable framework to share knowledge, and by easing further development of applications.

a comprehensive data model and ontology design patterns can be used to transform heterogeneous data sources into a coherent knowledge representation, which can be used to develop applications for smart cities, as well as to support the design of new smart city services.
the development of smart cities requires the integration of heterogeneous data sources, which is not a simple task.
